By Lemmas~\ref{lem:motif-family-lwbd} and~\ref{lem:subgraph}, the bounded degree motif family $\mathcal{M}(N_{\mathsf{v}},N_{\mathsf{e}},d)$ is \emph{$N_{\mathsf{e}}$-admissible}.
In view of Theorem~\ref{thm:bd-degree-motif-main}, if $\rho$ is a constant, one can choose a constant $N_{\mathsf{e}}$ when $p \ge n^{-2/3}$, making the test statistic computable in polynomial time. To obtain a more broadly applicable motif-counting statistic, we will show in Section~\ref{subsec:general-bd-degree} that counting all bounded degree motifs also suffices for correlation detection.

nodes.statement: As shown in Theorems~ and~, there exist conditions on N_e to satisfy the detection criterion 0.05. As shown in Theorems~\ref{thm:bd-degree-motif-main} and~\ref{thm:bd-degree-motif-general}, there exist conditions on $N_{\mathsf{e}}$ to satisfy the detection criterion $0.05$. 
To achieve stronger statistical efficiency, it is necessary to count motifs with a larger number of edges. Consequently, there exists a trade-off between computation time and statistical efficiency.
